intent.raw_query: Nepal trekking Annapurna, $2000 solo, October 2026, 14 days

experiences.name: Annapurna Base Camp Trek
experiences.description: Embark on the iconic multi-day trek to Annapurna Base Camp at 4,130m, passing through rhododendron forests, traditional Gurung villages, and dramatic mountain landscapes with stunning views of Annapurna I, Machapuchare, and Hiunchuli peaks.

experiences.name: Poon Hill Sunrise Hike
experiences.description: Rise before dawn and hike to Poon Hill viewpoint at 3,210m for one of Nepal's most celebrated panoramic sunrise views over the Annapurna and Dhaulagiri mountain ranges, with golden light illuminating the snow-capped peaks in a breathtaking display.

experiences.name: Gurung Village Cultural Homestay
experiences.description: Stay overnight in a traditional Gurung ethnic village, sharing meals of dal bhat and local millet raksi with host families, learning about ancient shamanic Bon and Buddhist traditions, and experiencing authentic mountain community life far from tourist trails.

experiences.name: Mardi Himal Trek to High Camp
experiences.description: Explore the lesser-trodden Mardi Himal trail through dense bamboo and rhododendron forests, ascending to High Camp at 3,580m for unobstructed close-up views of Machapuchare (Fishtail Mountain) and the Annapurna massif with far fewer crowds than the classic routes.

experiences.name: Birethanti to Tadapani Nature Walk
experiences.description: Trek through the lush lower Annapurna Conservation Area spotting diverse Himalayan wildlife including red pandas, langur monkeys, and over 100 bird species including the Danphe (Himalayan Monal), Nepal's national bird, while walking through ancient oak and rhododendron forests.
experiences.location: Birethanti to Tadapani, Modi Khola Corridor

trip_options.title: Budget Explorer - Annapurna, Nepal
trip_options.description: Save money without sacrificing the experience. Perfect for travelers who value authentic local experiences over luxury.

day_by_day.morning: No activities scheduled — flight arrives at 13:00
day_by_day.afternoon: Arrive at Tribhuvan International Airport, Kathmandu at 13:00. Clear customs and immigration, exchange currency at the airport (look for Nepal Rastra Bank counters for fair rates). Take a budget taxi or shared shuttle to Pokhara (or book an overnight bus if heading directly). If staying in Kathmandu overnight, check into a budget guesthouse in Thamel and take a short orientation walk around the neighborhood to get acquainted with local shops, stalls, and the vibrant street scene.
day_by_day.evening: Stroll through Thamel's lively streets. Visit a local tea shop for a welcome cup of Nepali milk tea (chiya). Pick up any last-minute trekking supplies at budget gear shops. Rest early to recover from travel.

meals.breakfast: Meal on the flight or airport snack
meals.lunch: Dal Bhat set meal at a local Thamel eatery (~300–400 NPR)
meals.dinner: Thakali Kitchen or similar local restaurant — try Nepali thali with lentil soup, rice, vegetables, and pickles (~400–500 NPR)

day_by_day.notes: Day 1 activities begin only after 13:00 arrival. Budget tip: Avoid tourist taxis at the airport — negotiate firmly or use prepaid taxi counters. Target spending: under $15 USD for the day excluding transport.

day_by_day.morning: Early morning bus or tourist coach from Kathmandu to Pokhara (7–8 hour journey, ~800–1000 NPR). Depart by 07:00 from Thamel bus park. Enjoy the scenic Prithvi Highway views along the Trishuli River valley. Pack snacks for the road.
day_by_day.afternoon: Arrive in Pokhara by mid-afternoon. Check into Aegean Bliss Resort in the Annapurna region. Freshen up and take a gentle lakeside walk along Phewa Lake (Fewa Tal) to stretch your legs after the long bus ride. Visit the local market near Lakeside (Baidam) to pick up any remaining trekking essentials.
day_by_day.evening: Watch the sunset over Phewa Lake with views of the Annapurna and Machhapuchhre (Fishtail) peaks reflected in the water. Visit Lakeside promenade for a relaxed evening stroll.

meals.breakfast: Light breakfast at Kathmandu guesthouse or packed snacks for the bus (~150–200 NPR)
meals.lunch: Roadside dhaba (local eatery) along the Prithvi Highway — dal bhat or noodle soup (~200–300 NPR)
meals.dinner: Momos (steamed dumplings) and vegetable curry at a Lakeside budget restaurant (~400–500 NPR)

day_by_day.notes: Book your Annapurna Conservation Area Permit (ACAP) and TIMS card today if not already arranged — available at the Nepal Tourism Board office in Pokhara (~3,000 NPR total for both). Essential for trekking.

day_by_day.morning: Early morning visit to the World Peace Pagoda (Shanti Stupa) — hike up the hill (about 45 minutes) or take a short boat ride across Phewa Lake followed by a 20-minute climb. Enjoy panoramic views of the Annapurna range and Pokhara valley at sunrise. Free entry to the pagoda.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit the International Mountain Museum in Pokhara (entry ~400 NPR) to learn about Himalayan geography, climbing history, and the cultures of mountain peoples — great preparation for your trek. Afterward, explore the Old Bazaar area for a taste of traditional Pokhara life.
day_by_day.evening: Return to the Lakeside area. Rent a rowboat on Phewa Lake for a peaceful evening paddle (~300–400 NPR per hour). Watch the alpenglow on the Annapurna peaks as the sun sets.

meals.breakfast: Porridge, eggs, and toast at a local teahouse near the resort (~200–300 NPR)
meals.lunch: Vegetable fried rice or chow mein at a local Lakeside café (~300–400 NPR)
meals.dinner: Nepali thali dinner at a budget local restaurant away from the main tourist strip (~400–500 NPR)

day_by_day.notes: This is your final preparation day before the trek begins. Repack your bag keeping it under 10–12 kg. Leave non-essential luggage at the resort's storage. Confirm your trekking permits are in order.

day_by_day.morning: Trek Day 1 — Pokhara to Tikhedhunga. Take a local bus or jeep from Pokhara to Nayapul (1.5–2 hours, ~200–300 NPR). Begin trekking from Nayapul through Modi Khola valley. Walk through terraced rice paddies, rhododendron forests, and small Gurung villages. Reach Birethanti for a permit check.
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue trekking uphill through Hille and Ulleri stone staircase (3,000+ stone steps — challenging but iconic). Arrive at Tikhedhunga (1,540m) by mid-afternoon. Check into a basic teahouse lodge (~300–500 NPR per night for a simple room).
day_by_day.evening: Relax at the teahouse, chat with fellow trekkers, and enjoy the mountain village atmosphere. Watch the stars from the open terrace — October skies are exceptionally clear.

meals.breakfast: Porridge and tea at the resort before departure (~200 NPR)
meals.lunch: Dal bhat at a teahouse in Birethanti or Hille (~400–500 NPR)
meals.dinner: Vegetable soup and dal bhat at Tikhedhunga teahouse (~400–500 NPR)

day_by_day.notes: October is peak trekking season — trails are busy but conditions are ideal with clear skies and stable weather. Stay hydrated and pace yourself on the Ulleri steps. Total trekking distance: ~14 km.

day_by_day.morning: Trek Day 2 — Tikhedhunga to Ghorepani. Early start at 07:00. Trek through dense rhododendron and oak forests. Pass through Banthanti and Nangethanti. The trail climbs steadily with beautiful forest scenery. October brings golden foliage and excellent visibility.
day_by_day.afternoon: Arrive at Ghorepani (2,860m) by early afternoon. Check into a teahouse. Rest and acclimatize to the altitude. Explore the small village, visit the local shops selling handmade crafts and warm gear.
day_by_day.evening: Sunset views of Dhaulagiri and Annapurna South from Ghorepani ridge. Warm up with a cup of ginger lemon honey tea by the teahouse fire. Meet fellow trekkers from around the world.

meals.breakfast: Tibetan bread with jam and tea at Tikhedhunga teahouse (~250–300 NPR)
meals.lunch: Noodle soup or fried rice at Banthanti teahouse (~400 NPR)
meals.dinner: Dal bhat with vegetable curry at Ghorepani teahouse (~500–600 NPR)

day_by_day.notes: Set your alarm for 04:30 tomorrow for the Poon Hill sunrise hike. Altitude at Ghorepani: 2,860m — some trekkers may feel mild breathlessness. Drink plenty of water and avoid alcohol. Total trekking: ~12 km.

day_by_day.morning: Pre-dawn hike to Poon Hill (3,210m) — depart at 05:00 with a headlamp. 45-minute uphill climb to the famous viewpoint. Witness one of the most spectacular Himalayan sunrises in Nepal with 360° views of Annapurna I, Annapurna South, Hiunchuli, Machhapuchhre, Dhaulagiri, and dozens more peaks. Entry fee: ~100 NPR. Return to Ghorepani for breakfast.
day_by_day.afternoon: Trek from Ghorepani to Tadapani (2,630m) through rhododendron forest. The trail offers continuous Annapurna range views. Arrive at Tadapani by mid-afternoon. Rest and enjoy the mountain panorama.
day_by_day.evening: Sunset views of Machhapuchhre (Fishtail Mountain) from Tadapani — arguably the best close-up view of this sacred unclimbed peak. Cozy evening at the teahouse.

meals.breakfast: Hot porridge, boiled eggs, and tea after Poon Hill return (~300–350 NPR)
meals.lunch: Snack bar or light meal at a trail teahouse (~300 NPR)
meals.dinner: Pumpkin soup and dal bhat at Tadapani teahouse (~500 NPR)

day_by_day.notes: Poon Hill is the highlight of the Annapurna Sanctuary/Ghorepani circuit. Bring warm layers — it can be below freezing at the viewpoint before sunrise. The October sky is typically crystal clear. Total trekking: ~10 km.

day_by_day.morning: Trek Day 4 — Tadapani to Chomrong (2,170m). Descend steeply through forest to the Modi Khola river, then climb up to the large Gurung village of Chomrong. Enjoy views of Annapurna South and Hiunchuli throughout the trail. Chomrong is a major gateway to the Annapurna Sanctuary (Base Camp).
day_by_day.afternoon: Arrive in Chomrong by early afternoon. Explore the village — one of the largest and most prosperous on the route. Visit the local gompa (Buddhist monastery). Check into a teahouse with panoramic mountain views.
day_by_day.evening: Enjoy the spectacular evening views of Annapurna South directly from Chomrong's terraces. The village lights up beautifully at dusk. Chat with local Gurung families.

meals.breakfast: Pancakes and honey with tea at Tadapani (~250–300 NPR)
meals.lunch: Dal bhat at a trail teahouse (~450–500 NPR)
meals.dinner: Garlic soup (great for altitude) and vegetable curry with rice at Chomrong teahouse (~500–600 NPR)

day_by_day.notes: Garlic is widely believed to help with altitude acclimatization — many trekkers order garlic soup regularly. Chomrong has reliable Wi-Fi at some teahouses (~200 NPR per hour). Total trekking: ~11 km.

day_by_day.morning: Trek Day 5 — Chomrong to Dovan (2,600m). Descend the famous Chomrong stone staircase to the Chomrong Khola river, then climb through bamboo and rhododendron forest. Pass through Sinuwa. The forest becomes increasingly dense and atmospheric — look for Himalayan wildlife including langur monkeys and colorful pheasants.
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue through Bamboo (2,310m) and onward to Dovan (2,600m). The trail follows the Modi Khola gorge with towering canyon walls. Arrive at Dovan's cluster of teahouses by mid-afternoon. The gorge creates a dramatic, almost mystical atmosphere.
day_by_day.evening: Rest at the teahouse. The gorge walls block direct sunlight by late afternoon, making evenings cool. Gather around the communal fire with fellow trekkers. Listen to the roaring Modi Khola river.

meals.breakfast: Porridge and tea at Chomrong teahouse (~250 NPR)
meals.lunch: Noodle soup at Sinuwa or Bamboo teahouse (~400–450 NPR)
meals.dinner: Dal bhat and vegetable curry at Dovan teahouse (~500 NPR)

day_by_day.notes: Note that prices increase as you go higher into the sanctuary — this is normal and expected due to porter supply costs. Budget approximately 20–30% more per meal from here onward. Total trekking: ~10 km.

day_by_day.morning: Trek Day 6 — Dovan to Machhapuchhre Base Camp (MBC) (3,700m). Pass through Himalaya Hotel (2,920m) and Deurali (3,230m). The vegetation thins dramatically as you gain altitude. Enter the high alpine zone with sweeping views of Hiunchuli, Annapurna South, and the Machhapuchhre massif towering above.
day_by_day.afternoon: Arrive at Machhapuchhre Base Camp (3,700m) — a dramatic high-altitude plateau surrounded by giant peaks. Check into a teahouse. Rest and acclimatize carefully. The air is noticeably thinner here. Drink water consistently.
day_by_day.evening: Watch the alpenglow on Machhapuchhre (6,993m) — the sacred Fishtail Mountain that has never been officially summited. The colors at sunset (orange, pink, purple on white peaks) are extraordinary. Wrap up warmly — temperatures can drop to -5°C or below at night.

meals.breakfast: Porridge and boiled eggs at Dovan (~300 NPR)
meals.lunch: Hot noodle soup or fried rice at Himalaya Hotel teahouse (~500–600 NPR)
meals.dinner: Dal bhat and garlic soup at MBC teahouse (~600–700 NPR)

day_by_day.notes: Altitude sickness risk increases significantly above 3,000m. Watch for symptoms: headache, nausea, dizziness, loss of appetite. If symptoms are severe, descend immediately. Carry altitude sickness medication (Diamox) if prescribed. Total trekking: ~11 km.

day_by_day.morning: Trek Day 7 — MBC to Annapurna Base Camp (ABC) (4,130m). Early morning departure at 06:00 to reach ABC for sunrise. The 2-hour trail crosses a high glacial moraine. As you crest the final ridge, the full Annapurna Sanctuary amphitheater is revealed — a 360° circle of 7,000–8,000m peaks including Annapurna I (8,091m, world's 10th highest). A truly life-changing moment.
day_by_day.afternoon: Spend the afternoon at ABC exploring the sanctuary. Walk around the moraine, photograph the glaciers, and soak in the unparalleled mountain scenery. Visit the memorial plaques for mountaineers who perished on Annapurna. Begin descent back toward MBC.
day_by_day.evening: Return to MBC or continue down to Deurali for the night. Celebrate reaching ABC with fellow trekkers. The sense of achievement is immense.

meals.breakfast: Light snack before dawn departure — biscuits and tea (~150 NPR)
meals.lunch: Hot soup and noodles at ABC teahouse (~600–700 NPR)
meals.dinner: Dal bhat at MBC or Deurali teahouse (~600 NPR)

day_by_day.notes: ABC at 4,130m is the pinnacle of this trek. October conditions are typically excellent with minimal snow on the trail. Start early to avoid afternoon cloud buildup. Carry sun protection — UV radiation is intense at altitude. Total trekking: ~8–14 km depending on descent.

day_by_day.morning: Trek Day 8 — Descent: Deurali/MBC to Bamboo (2,310m). A long but satisfying descent retracing the route through the Modi Khola gorge. Your legs will feel the downhill — use trekking poles to protect knees. The forest feels lush and oxygen-rich after the high altitude.
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue descent through Sinuwa toward Bamboo or Chomrong. The trail feels much more manageable on the way down. Enjoy the forest sounds — birdsong, waterfalls, wind through bamboo.
day_by_day.evening: Arrive at Bamboo or Chomrong teahouse. Hot shower if available (~200–300 NPR extra). Celebrate the successful ABC trek with a special dinner.

meals.breakfast: Porridge and tea at starting teahouse (~300 NPR)
meals.lunch: Dal bhat at Himalaya Hotel or Dovan (~500 NPR)
meals.dinner: Vegetable curry, rice, and lentil soup — treat yourself to a slightly larger meal to replenish energy (~600 NPR)

day_by_day.notes: Descents are harder on joints than ascents. Take your time, step carefully on wet rocks, and use poles. Total descent: approximately 1,800m elevation drop. Total trekking: ~16 km.

day_by_day.morning: Trek Day 9 — Chomrong to Jhinu Danda (1,780m) and natural hot springs. Descend from Chomrong through the Modi Khola valley. Take the side trail down to Jhinu Danda's famous natural hot springs on the riverbank. Soak aching trekking muscles in the geothermal pools — one of the best rewards after a long trek (~200 NPR entry).
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue trekking or rest at Jhinu Danda. Optional: continue to New Bridge and Siwai. Begin the final descent toward the Nayapul/Birethanti trailhead area.
day_by_day.evening: Arrive at a lower village teahouse — Landruk or Tolka. Enjoy the warmer temperatures at lower altitude. Celebrate the near-completion of the trek.

meals.breakfast: Tibetan bread and honey with tea at Chomrong (~250–300 NPR)
meals.lunch: Noodle soup at a trail teahouse (~400 NPR)
meals.dinner: Dal bhat with extra vegetables and pickle at Landruk/Tolka teahouse (~500 NPR)

day_by_day.notes: Jhinu Danda hot springs are a beloved tradition for trekkers finishing the Annapurna Sanctuary route. Don't miss them! The springs are open from approximately 07:00–18:00. Total trekking: ~12 km.

day_by_day.morning: Final Trek Day — Descend to Nayapul and return to Pokhara. Early morning departure, trekking through terraced fields and Gurung villages with beautiful valley views. Pass through Birethanti for a final permit check. Reach Nayapul by mid-morning.
day_by_day.afternoon: Take a local bus or jeep from Nayapul back to Pokhara (~200–300 NPR, 1.5 hours). Return to Aegean Bliss Resort. Enjoy a long hot shower and rest. Afternoon: gentle lakeside walk along Phewa Lake to decompress. Optional: boat ride on the lake to celebrate.
day_by_day.evening: Celebration dinner at a Lakeside restaurant. Reflect on the incredible 10-day trekking adventure. Browse the lakeside shops for last-minute souvenirs — handmade Nepali crafts, Thangka paintings, pashmina scarves (bargain respectfully).

meals.breakfast: Porridge and tea at final teahouse (~250 NPR)
meals.lunch: Dal bhat at Birethanti or roadside dhaba in Nayapul (~400 NPR)
meals.dinner: Celebration meal — try a wood-fired pizza or mixed Nepali-Western meal at a Lakeside budget restaurant (~600–800 NPR)

day_by_day.notes: You've completed the Annapurna Sanctuary Trek — approximately 110+ km over 10 days! This is a major achievement. Take care of any blisters or minor injuries. Visit a pharmacy in Pokhara if needed — basic medical supplies are affordable.

day_by_day.morning: Final morning in Pokhara — sunrise over the Annapurna range from the lakeside promenade (no hiking required!). Take a peaceful rowboat on Phewa Lake and visit the Barahi Temple on the lake island (small boat fee ~200 NPR, temple donation optional). Enjoy a leisurely breakfast.
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore the Seti River George viewpoints near Pokhara — a dramatic natural canyon where the Seti Gandaki River flows underground. Free to visit. Visit the Bindhyabasini Temple for a cultural experience. Final souvenir shopping at the Old Bazaar for the best local prices on handcrafts.
day_by_day.evening: Return to Kathmandu by evening tourist bus or flight (book in advance — Pokhara to Kathmandu flight ~$80–100 USD or bus ~1,000 NPR). If flying out on Day 15, stay overnight in Kathmandu. Final dinner in Thamel — try the famous Nepali set meal with raksi (local millet spirit) for a proper farewell.

meals.breakfast: Full Nepali breakfast — sel roti (rice flour doughnut), aloo tarkari (spiced potatoes), and chiya tea at a local café (~300–400 NPR)
meals.lunch: Thakali thali at a restaurant near the lakeside (~500 NPR)
meals.dinner: Farewell dinner in Thamel, Kathmandu — Nepali cuisine with momo, dal bhat, and lassi (~600–800 NPR)

day_by_day.notes: Budget summary for the 14-day trip: Accommodation ~$3–7/night at teahouses + resort; Meals ~$5–10/day on trek; Permits (ACAP + TIMS) ~$30 USD total; Transport ~$20–30 USD total; Miscellaneous ~$20–30 USD. Estimated total budget: $250–350 USD for the trekking portion, excluding international flights. Nepal is one of the world's most affordable trekking destinations — enjoy every moment!

trip_options.title: Classic Annapurna, Nepal Experience
trip_options.description: The sweet spot between comfort and value. Enjoy quality accommodations, diverse experiences, and good food.

day_by_day.morning: No activities scheduled — flight arrives at 13:00
day_by_day.afternoon: Arrive at Tribhuvan International Airport, Kathmandu. Complete immigration and baggage claim, then take a pre-arranged transfer or tourist bus toward Pokhara (gateway to Annapurna). Enjoy scenic highway views of the Himalayan foothills en route (~6-7 hours) or take a domestic flight to Pokhara if available. Check in to Aegean Bliss Resort upon arrival and freshen up.
day_by_day.evening: Stroll along Phewa Lake promenade near Pokhara lakeside. Enjoy the calm waterfront atmosphere, browse local souvenir shops, and take in first views of the Annapurna range at dusk.

meals.breakfast: Meal on board or at Kathmandu airport — grab a quick bite at a café such as Himalayan Java Coffee
meals.lunch: Pack a light snack for the journey or stop at a roadside dhaba (local eatery) along the Prithvi Highway for dal bhat (~$3-5)
meals.dinner: Moondance Restaurant, Pokhara Lakeside — popular mid-range spot with Nepali and continental options (~$8-12 per person)

day_by_day.notes: Day 1 is primarily a travel and arrival day. Rest well — acclimatization begins now. Avoid alcohol on the first night. Confirm trek permits and gear rental plans with hotel staff.

day_by_day.morning: Early morning visit to Sarangkot Hill (30-min drive from Pokhara) for a breathtaking sunrise over the Annapurna and Dhaulagiri mountain ranges. Arrive before 6:00 AM for the best views. Light hiking on the hilltop trails.
day_by_day.afternoon: Return to Pokhara and visit the International Mountain Museum to learn about Himalayan geology, climbing history, and local culture. Afterward, rent a rowboat or kayak on Phewa Lake and paddle toward the Tal Barahi Temple on the island.
day_by_day.evening: Explore the Lakeside Bazaar (Baidam area) for trekking gear, maps, and local crafts. Attend a traditional Nepali cultural show if available at a local venue.

meals.breakfast: Hotel breakfast or Busy Bee Café, Lakeside — eggs, toast, fresh fruit, and coffee (~$4-6)
meals.lunch: New Everest Steak House, Lakeside — hearty sandwiches, soups, and Nepali set meals (~$6-9)
meals.dinner: Caffe Concerto, Lakeside — wood-fired pizza, pasta, and Nepali dishes in a relaxed setting (~$8-12)

day_by_day.notes: Use today to finalize trekking permits: TIMS Card (Trekkers' Information Management System) and ACAP (Annapurna Conservation Area Permit) — both obtainable at the Nepal Tourism Board office in Pokhara. Budget ~$30-40 USD total for permits.

day_by_day.morning: Drive or take a local jeep from Pokhara to Nayapul (1.5-2 hours). Begin the Annapurna Circuit/Sanctuary trek from Nayapul, hiking through terraced rice fields and rhododendron forests toward Tikhedhunga (approx. 4-5 hours trekking, moderate difficulty).
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue trekking to Ulleri if energy allows, climbing the famous stone staircase of 3,000+ steps through lush forest. Arrive at a teahouse in Ulleri or Tikhedhunga and rest. Enjoy panoramic valley views.
day_by_day.evening: Settle into a mid-range teahouse lodge. Socialize with fellow trekkers in the common dining area. Enjoy warm tea and the peaceful mountain atmosphere.

meals.breakfast: Hotel breakfast before departure — porridge, eggs, and tea
meals.lunch: Teahouse meal in Tikhedhunga — dal bhat or noodle soup (~$4-6)
meals.dinner: Teahouse dinner in Ulleri — dal bhat set meal (the trekker's staple, unlimited refills, ~$5-7)

day_by_day.notes: Trek distance: ~10-12 km. Elevation gain: ~1,400m to ~1,960m. Wear layered clothing as temperatures drop in the evening. Carry 2-3 liters of water and water purification tablets.

day_by_day.morning: Early start from Ulleri, trekking through oak and rhododendron forests toward Ghorepani (approx. 3-4 hours). The trail passes through traditional Magar villages with stunning mountain backdrops.
day_by_day.afternoon: Arrive at Ghorepani (2,860m) by early afternoon. Rest and acclimatize. Explore the village, visit local tea shops, and interact with Gurung and Magar community members. Optional short hike to viewpoints above the village.
day_by_day.evening: Warm up by the teahouse fire. Enjoy views of Dhaulagiri and Annapurna South at sunset from the village edge. Prepare gear for the pre-dawn Poon Hill hike the next morning.

meals.breakfast: Teahouse breakfast — pancakes with honey, porridge, or eggs and toast (~$3-5)
meals.lunch: Packed lunch or teahouse stop en route — vegetable noodle soup or fried rice (~$4-6)
meals.dinner: Ghorepani teahouse — dal bhat or vegetable curry with rice (~$5-8)

day_by_day.notes: Trek distance: ~8 km. Altitude increases significantly — watch for early signs of altitude sickness (headache, nausea). Stay hydrated. Set alarm for 4:30 AM for the Poon Hill sunrise hike tomorrow.

day_by_day.morning: Pre-dawn hike to Poon Hill (3,210m) — depart at 5:00 AM with a headlamp for a 45-minute climb. Witness one of Nepal's most iconic sunrises over the Annapurna and Dhaulagiri ranges. Return to Ghorepani for breakfast.
day_by_day.afternoon: Trek from Ghorepani to Tadapani through dense rhododendron and oak forest (approx. 4-5 hours). The trail offers continuous mountain views and diverse birdlife including Himalayan monals.
day_by_day.evening: Arrive at Tadapani (2,590m). Enjoy sunset views of Annapurna South and Hiunchuli from the village. Rest and enjoy the quieter, less-commercialized teahouse atmosphere.

meals.breakfast: Post-Poon Hill breakfast at Ghorepani teahouse — eggs, toast, porridge, hot lemon tea (~$4-6)
meals.lunch: Packed snacks or brief teahouse stop en route — energy bars, nuts, and tea
meals.dinner: Tadapani teahouse — garlic soup (great for altitude), dal bhat or pasta (~$5-8)

day_by_day.notes: Poon Hill is the highlight of the Ghorepani-Poon Hill circuit — one of the most photographed Himalayan viewpoints. Bring a warm jacket as pre-dawn temperatures can drop to 0°C in October. Trek distance today: ~12 km total.

day_by_day.morning: Trek from Tadapani toward Chhomrong (approx. 4-5 hours), descending through forests and crossing suspension bridges over the Modi Khola river. Chhomrong is the main gateway village to the Annapurna Sanctuary.
day_by_day.afternoon: Arrive at Chhomrong (2,170m). Explore this large Gurung village, visit the local gompa (Buddhist monastery), and enjoy panoramic views of Annapurna South and Hiunchuli directly ahead.
day_by_day.evening: Relax at a comfortable mid-range teahouse with a garden terrace. Enjoy the best mountain views of the trek so far. Chat with locals about Gurung culture and traditions.

meals.breakfast: Tadapani teahouse — pancakes, eggs, and hot chocolate (~$4-6)
meals.lunch: Teahouse in Sinuwa or en route — dal bhat or noodle soup (~$4-6)
meals.dinner: Chhomrong teahouse — apple pie (locally famous), dal bhat, and ginger lemon honey tea (~$6-9)

day_by_day.notes: Trek distance: ~10 km. Chhomrong has the last reliable ATM and medical post before the upper sanctuary. Withdraw sufficient Nepali Rupees here. Stock up on snacks and water purification supplies.

day_by_day.morning: Trek from Chhomrong into the Annapurna Sanctuary via Sinuwa and Bamboo (approx. 4-5 hours). The trail descends steeply into the Modi Khola gorge then climbs through dense bamboo and rhododendron forest.
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue trekking to Dovan or Himalaya Hotel (approx. 2 more hours). The landscape becomes increasingly dramatic as the valley narrows and the towering walls of Annapurna South and Hiunchuli close in around you.
day_by_day.evening: Rest at a teahouse in Himalaya Hotel settlement (2,920m). The atmosphere is remote and atmospheric — you are now deep inside the Annapurna Sanctuary. Enjoy the sounds of the river and mountain silence.

meals.breakfast: Chhomrong teahouse — eggs, toast, and porridge (~$4-6)
meals.lunch: Bamboo teahouse — dal bhat or instant noodles (~$4-6)
meals.dinner: Himalaya Hotel teahouse — dal bhat, vegetable curry, and hot lemon tea (~$5-8)

day_by_day.notes: Trek distance: ~14 km. This is the most demanding day so far. The trail can be slippery — use trekking poles. Leeches may be present in forested sections in October — tuck trousers into socks. Altitude increases sharply.

day_by_day.morning: Trek from Himalaya Hotel to Annapurna Base Camp (ABC) via Machhapuchhre Base Camp (MBC) — approx. 5-6 hours total. The trail opens into the glacial amphitheater of the Annapurna Sanctuary with 360-degree views of Annapurna I (8,091m), Annapurna South, Gangapurna, and Machhapuchhre (Fishtail).
day_by_day.afternoon: Arrive at Annapurna Base Camp (4,130m). Take time to absorb the extraordinary surroundings — a natural ice and rock amphitheater ringed by some of the world's highest peaks. Explore the base camp area and take photographs.
day_by_day.evening: Watch the sunset alpenglow turn the Annapurna massif golden and pink. This is the emotional and scenic peak of the entire trip. Celebrate with fellow trekkers over tea and dinner.

meals.breakfast: Himalaya Hotel teahouse — porridge with honey, eggs, and tea (~$4-6)
meals.lunch: MBC teahouse — hot soup, fried rice, or dal bhat (~$5-7)
meals.dinner: ABC teahouse — dal bhat (essential for energy at altitude), hot chocolate or ginger tea (~$7-10)

day_by_day.notes: MILESTONE DAY — reaching Annapurna Base Camp at 4,130m. Altitude sickness risk is real: move slowly, drink 4+ liters of water, avoid alcohol. If symptoms worsen (severe headache, vomiting, confusion), descend immediately. Temperature at night can drop to -10°C — use all available blankets.

day_by_day.morning: Wake before sunrise for the spectacular dawn light on the Annapurna massif from base camp — one of the most breathtaking mountain panoramas on Earth. Spend the morning exploring and photographing the glacial moraine and surrounding peaks.
day_by_day.afternoon: Begin descent from ABC back toward MBC and Deurali (approx. 4-5 hours descending). The return journey feels faster and the lower altitude brings renewed energy.
day_by_day.evening: Rest at a teahouse in Deurali or Himalaya Hotel. Enjoy the warmer temperatures at lower elevation. Reflect on the ABC experience over a warm meal.

meals.breakfast: ABC teahouse — porridge, eggs, and hot drinks (~$5-7)
meals.lunch: MBC or Deurali teahouse — noodle soup, fried rice (~$4-6)
meals.dinner: Himalaya Hotel or Dovan teahouse — dal bhat, vegetable curry (~$5-8)

day_by_day.notes: Descend carefully — knees take the most strain on the way down. Use trekking poles and take it slow on steep sections. The descent to lower altitudes will significantly improve sleep quality and appetite.

day_by_day.morning: Continue descent from Dovan/Himalaya Hotel back through Bamboo and Sinuwa to Chhomrong (approx. 5-6 hours). The forest trail is beautiful in the morning light with birdsong and mountain views.
day_by_day.afternoon: Arrive back in Chhomrong. Take a well-deserved rest. Optional: visit the local hot spring at Jhinu Danda (1 hour detour below Chhomrong) for a soak in natural thermal pools — perfect for tired trekking legs.
day_by_day.evening: Enjoy dinner at Chhomrong with views of Annapurna South. Treat yourself to the famous local apple products — apple pie, apple brandy, or apple cider.

meals.breakfast: Dovan teahouse — eggs, toast, porridge (~$4-6)
meals.lunch: Sinuwa teahouse — dal bhat or noodle soup (~$4-6)
meals.dinner: Chhomrong teahouse — grilled vegetables, dal bhat, and Nepali apple brandy (~$7-10)

day_by_day.notes: Jhinu Danda hot springs cost ~$3-5 entry. Bring a towel and change of clothes. The hot spring soak is highly recommended after 8 days of trekking — muscles will thank you. Trek distance today: ~12 km.

day_by_day.morning: Trek from Chhomrong back toward Ghandruk — a beautiful large Gurung village (approx. 3-4 hours). The trail passes through terraced fields with outstanding views of Annapurna South and Machhapuchhre.
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore Ghandruk village — visit the Gurung Museum to learn about local culture, traditional architecture, and the famous Gurkha warrior heritage. Walk the stone-paved lanes between traditional stone houses.
day_by_day.evening: Enjoy sunset views from Ghandruk's hilltop viewpoints. This is one of the most picturesque villages in the Annapurna region. Relax at a comfortable teahouse with garden views.

meals.breakfast: Chhomrong teahouse — pancakes, eggs, and coffee (~$4-6)
meals.lunch: Trail teahouse or Ghandruk arrival meal — dal bhat or pasta (~$4-7)
meals.dinner: Ghandruk teahouse — Gurung-style local cuisine, nettle soup, and corn bread (~$6-9)

day_by_day.notes: Ghandruk is one of the most authentic Gurung villages in Nepal and a highlight of the cultural side of the Annapurna trek. The Gurung Museum (small entry fee ~$1-2) is excellent. Trek distance: ~8 km.

day_by_day.morning: Trek from Ghandruk down to Kimche and take a local jeep back to Pokhara (approx. 2 hours trekking + 1.5 hours drive). Alternatively, trek the full route to Nayapul and drive back. Arrive in Pokhara by midday.
day_by_day.afternoon: Return to Aegean Bliss Resort. Enjoy a long hot shower, laundry service, and full rest. Optional: therapeutic massage at a Pokhara spa to recover from the trek (~$15-25 for 60-minute full body massage at mid-range spas).
day_by_day.evening: Celebrate completing the Annapurna trek with a proper sit-down dinner at one of Pokhara's better restaurants. Enjoy the lakeside atmosphere and reflect on the journey.

meals.breakfast: Ghandruk teahouse — full trekkers' breakfast (~$4-6)
meals.lunch: Pokhara Lakeside restaurant — proper meal with salad, main course, and dessert (~$8-12)
meals.dinner: Olive Garden Restaurant, Pokhara — Nepali thali, grilled meats, or international cuisine with lake views (~$10-15)

day_by_day.notes: Jeep from Kimche to Pokhara costs ~$5-8 per person in shared jeep. After 10 days of teahouse food, Pokhara's restaurant variety will feel luxurious. Book a massage in advance at busy season. Rest is essential before final days.

day_by_day.morning: Relaxed morning at the resort. Optional sunrise boat ride on Phewa Lake for reflections of the Annapurna range on the still water — one of Nepal's most iconic images. Visit the Barahi Temple on the lake island.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit the World Peace Pagoda (Shanti Stupa) — a 45-minute hike or short boat ride + hike above Phewa Lake. Stunning 360-degree views of Pokhara, the lake, and the Annapurna range. Explore the Davis Falls and Gupteshwor Cave nearby.
day_by_day.evening: Final evening in the Annapurna region. Browse Lakeside market for last-minute souvenirs: Thangka paintings, pashmina scarves, handmade jewelry, and trekking memorabilia. Enjoy a farewell dinner.

meals.breakfast: Resort or Lakeside café — full Western or Nepali breakfast (~$5-8)
meals.lunch: Café du Mont, Pokhara — sandwiches, salads, and fresh juices in a relaxed setting (~$7-10)
meals.dinner: Lemon Tree Restaurant, Pokhara — upscale Nepali and continental cuisine, great for a celebratory last dinner (~$12-18)

day_by_day.notes: World Peace Pagoda hike takes about 1-1.5 hours round trip — wear comfortable shoes. Davis Falls is free to enter. Souvenir shopping tip: bargaining is expected and acceptable — aim for 20-30% off initial asking prices.

day_by_day.morning: Final morning in Pokhara. Enjoy a leisurely breakfast at the resort. Last walk along the Phewa Lake promenade. Pack and prepare for departure. Optional: short sunrise hike or final kayak session on the lake.
day_by_day.afternoon: Check out from Aegean Bliss Resort. Transfer to Pokhara Airport for domestic flight to Kathmandu, or take the tourist bus/private vehicle (~6-7 hours). If time permits in Kathmandu, visit Pashupatinath Temple or Boudhanath Stupa before the international departure.
day_by_day.evening: Depart from Tribhuvan International Airport, Kathmandu. Carry fond memories of the Annapurna Himalaya, the warmth of Nepali hospitality, and the achievement of reaching Annapurna Base Camp.

meals.breakfast: Resort breakfast — full spread to fuel the travel day (~$6-8)
meals.lunch: Pokhara airport café or packed lunch for the journey (~$4-7)
meals.dinner: Kathmandu airport restaurant or in-flight meal — Nepali set meal or international options (~$8-15)

day_by_day.notes: Allow at least 3 hours before international departure for check-in, security, and immigration at Kathmandu. Domestic Pokhara-Kathmandu flights are 25 minutes but can be delayed by weather — book an early flight. Confirm return flight details and carry all trekking permits as souvenirs.

highlights: Mix of paid and free experiences

trip_options.title: Premium Annapurna, Nepal Escape
trip_options.description: Indulge in the best the destination has to offer. Premium flights, luxury hotels, and exclusive experiences.

day_by_day.morning: Arrival at Tribhuvan International Airport at 13:00 — no morning activities scheduled
day_by_day.afternoon: Private luxury transfer from Kathmandu airport to Pokhara via scenic mountain highway or chartered helicopter flight over the Himalayas for a breathtaking aerial introduction to the Annapurna range. Check in to Aegean Bliss Resort, unpack and settle into your premium suite with Annapurna panoramic views.
day_by_day.evening: Leisurely stroll along the Phewa Lake shoreline near the resort. Enjoy a welcome cocktail at the resort's rooftop bar as the alpenglow lights up Machhapuchhre (Fishtail Mountain) and the Annapurna massif at sunset.

meals.breakfast: Not applicable — in-flight or airport lounge meal
meals.lunch: Light refreshment at Kathmandu airport premium lounge or en route at a curated mountain-view café in Pokhara
meals.dinner: Private welcome dinner at the resort's signature restaurant featuring Newari and contemporary Nepali cuisine paired with Himalayan herbal cocktails and local Mustang apple wine

day_by_day.notes: Acclimatization begins here — Pokhara sits at approximately 820m. Hydrate well, rest early, and avoid strenuous activity on arrival day. Confirm all trekking permits and gear with your dedicated resort concierge this evening.

day_by_day.morning: Sunrise yoga session on the resort's private deck overlooking the Annapurna range led by a certified Himalayan yoga instructor. Follow with a guided 3-hour nature walk around Phewa Lake's forested northern shore, spotting rhododendron groves and Himalayan bird species including the danphe (national bird of Nepal).
day_by_day.afternoon: Private boat excursion on Phewa Lake to the sacred Tal Barahi Temple on its island, followed by a leisurely paddle to the far shore for a guided exploration of the World Peace Pagoda (Shanti Stupa) perched 1,113m above the lake with sweeping Annapurna panoramas.
day_by_day.evening: Sunset cocktails at the resort's lakeside terrace. Cultural performance of traditional Gurung and Tharu folk dances arranged exclusively for premium guests.

meals.breakfast: Lavish Himalayan breakfast buffet at the resort featuring fresh local honey, organic Nepali cheese, buckwheat pancakes, and seasonal mountain fruits
meals.lunch: Gourmet picnic basket prepared by the resort chef enjoyed at the World Peace Pagoda viewpoint
meals.dinner: Fine dining at Pokhara's acclaimed Moondance Restaurant or resort in-house chef's tasting menu with Himalayan trout, yak cheese platters, and dal bhat reimagined with premium ingredients

day_by_day.notes: October is peak trekking season in Nepal — skies are typically crystal clear with excellent mountain visibility. Carry sunscreen and a light layer for the boat excursion. Confirm Day 4 trekking permits with concierge today.

day_by_day.morning: Pre-dawn private jeep transfer to Sarangkot Hill (1,592m) for one of Nepal's most spectacular Himalayan sunrises — panoramic views of Annapurna I, II, III, IV, Machhapuchhre, Dhaulagiri, and Manaslu. Guided photography session with a professional mountain photographer provided.
day_by_day.afternoon: Return to resort for a late luxury brunch. Afternoon guided cultural tour of Pokhara's Old Bazaar, Bindhyabasini Temple, and the Gurkha Museum, exploring the rich heritage of Nepal's legendary soldiers with a private historian guide.
day_by_day.evening: Relaxing spa treatment at the resort's Himalayan wellness center — choose from a traditional Ayurvedic massage, hot stone therapy with Himalayan salt, or a full aromatherapy body wrap using locally sourced herbs. Prepare gear for tomorrow's trek departure.

meals.breakfast: Light pre-dawn snack box prepared by the resort (thermos of Nepali masala tea, energy bars, fresh fruit) before Sarangkot departure
meals.lunch: Extended brunch back at the resort post-sunrise: eggs Benedict, smoked Himalayan trout, fresh juices, and artisan Nepali coffee
meals.dinner: Intimate candlelit dinner at the resort's private garden terrace, featuring a four-course menu with Annapurna valley seasonal vegetables, yak tenderloin, and momo dumplings elevated with truffle and local spices

day_by_day.notes: Sarangkot departure is typically at 04:30–05:00 for optimal sunrise timing. Dress warmly — temperatures at the viewpoint can drop to 5–8°C before dawn in October. This is the final full rest day before multi-day trekking begins.

day_by_day.morning: Early luxury jeep transfer to Nayapul (1,070m) — the classic starting point of the Annapurna Sanctuary and Poon Hill circuit. Begin guided trek through terraced rice paddies and rhododendron forests toward Tikhedhunga (1,540m). Private certified mountain guide and personal porter service included.
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue trekking through the Modi Khola river valley, ascending stone-paved trails through the traditional Magar village of Ulleri (1,960m) — one of the most iconic stone staircase climbs in the Annapurna region with over 3,000 steps through lush forest.
day_by_day.evening: Arrive at Ghorepani (2,860m). Check in to the finest premium teahouse lodge available — Trekkers Inn or equivalent luxury teahouse with private en-suite rooms, heated blankets, and mountain-view terraces. Acclimatization walk around the village.

meals.breakfast: Full hot breakfast at the resort before departure: porridge, eggs, toast, and Nepali tea
meals.lunch: Gourmet trail lunch at a curated rest stop in Tikhedhunga — dal bhat, fresh vegetable curry, and lemon honey tea
meals.dinner: Hearty premium teahouse dinner in Ghorepani: garlic soup, vegetable stir-fry with noodles, apple crumble, and Himalayan herbal tea — all locally sourced ingredients

day_by_day.notes: Today's trek is approximately 12km and 6–7 hours of walking. Altitude gain is significant — stay well hydrated and maintain a slow, steady pace. Porter will carry main luggage; carry only a day pack. Ghorepani at 2,860m may feel cool to cold at night (2–5°C). Confirm 04:00 wake-up call for Poon Hill sunrise tomorrow.

day_by_day.morning: Pre-dawn guided hike to Poon Hill viewpoint (3,210m) — the crown jewel of the Annapurna region, offering a legendary 360-degree panorama of over a dozen Himalayan peaks above 7,000m including Dhaulagiri, Annapurna South, Hiunchuli, and Machhapuchhre bathed in golden alpenglow. Professional sunrise photography session included.
day_by_day.afternoon: Descend back to Ghorepani for breakfast, then continue trekking through dense rhododendron and oak forests via Deurali (3,100m) toward Tadapani (2,630m), passing through one of the most biodiverse forest corridors in the Annapurna Conservation Area.
day_by_day.evening: Arrive Tadapani. Settle into premium teahouse accommodation. Enjoy the extraordinary close-up views of Annapurna South and Hiunchuli directly above the village. Guided evening star-gazing session with a Himalayan astronomy guide — October skies offer exceptional clarity.

meals.breakfast: Hot tea and energy snacks at Poon Hill summit, followed by a full hot breakfast back at the Ghorepani lodge
meals.lunch: Trail lunch at a forest clearing between Deurali and Tadapani — packed gourmet lunch box with sandwiches, local cheese, nuts, chocolate, and fresh fruit
meals.dinner: Premium teahouse dinner in Tadapani: Nepali thali with multiple curries, lentil soup, sautéed mountain greens, rice, and warm apple cider

day_by_day.notes: Poon Hill departure is at 04:30 — it is a 45-minute uphill walk in darkness; bring a headlamp. October temperatures at Poon Hill summit can reach -5°C before dawn — dress in full thermal layers. Today's total trekking distance is approximately 10km.

day_by_day.morning: Morning guided trek from Tadapani through ancient rhododendron forests — these trees are among the oldest and largest in Nepal, some over 400 years old. Descend via Gurjung to Chhomrong (2,170m), a charming Gurung village with spectacular close-range views of Annapurna South and Machhapuchhre.
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore Chhomrong village — visit the local Gurung community center, observe traditional stone house architecture, and learn about Gurung shamanic traditions with a private cultural guide. Optional short hike to a nearby waterfall viewpoint above the village.
day_by_day.evening: Sunset views of Annapurna South from Chhomrong's famous stone terraces. Check in to the best available premium lodge in Chhomrong with private rooms and hot shower facilities. Briefing from guide about the upcoming Annapurna Base Camp approach.

meals.breakfast: Hot porridge, eggs, and Nepali tea at Tadapani lodge
meals.lunch: Lunch at a traditional teahouse in Gurjung mid-trail — fresh tomato soup, fried rice, and seasonal vegetables
meals.dinner: Chhomrong teahouse dinner: grilled Himalayan cheese on toast, vegetable curry, fresh yak butter tea, and homemade apple pie — a Chhomrong specialty

day_by_day.notes: Today's trek is approximately 8–9km with significant descent and re-ascent. Chhomrong is the last major village before the Annapurna Sanctuary — stock up on any needed snacks or supplies at the village shops. The Annapurna Conservation Area checkpoint is here; ensure permits are stamped.

day_by_day.morning: Trek from Chhomrong descending to the Modi Khola river and ascending through bamboo and rhododendron forests to Sinuwa (2,360m) and Bamboo (2,310m). The trail enters the dramatic inner gorge of the Annapurna Sanctuary — towering walls of rock and forest on both sides.
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue through Dovan (2,600m) and Himalaya Hotel (2,920m), trekking deeper into the sanctuary gorge. The vegetation shifts from dense forest to alpine scrub as altitude increases. Watch for Himalayan tahr (wild mountain goat), monal pheasants, and if lucky, snow leopard tracks.
day_by_day.evening: Arrive at Deurali (3,230m). Premium teahouse check-in. The sanctuary walls begin to open above — on clear October evenings the first glimpses of the Annapurna glacier amphitheater become visible. Early rest is essential for acclimatization.

meals.breakfast: Full hot breakfast at Chhomrong lodge before departure
meals.lunch: Hot lunch at Himalaya Hotel teahouse: garlic noodle soup, vegetable fried rice, and ginger lemon honey tea
meals.dinner: Deurali teahouse dinner: hearty pasta with tomato sauce, vegetable curry, hot chocolate, and altitude-friendly light dessert

day_by_day.notes: Today's trek covers approximately 11km and 6–7 hours of walking with significant altitude gain. At 3,230m, altitude sickness symptoms may begin for some trekkers — headache, mild nausea, and fatigue are normal. If symptoms are severe, descend immediately. Drink 3–4 liters of water today. No alcohol at altitude.

day_by_day.morning: Early morning trek from Deurali — the sanctuary walls dramatically open to reveal the full Annapurna amphitheater. Pass Machhapuchhre Base Camp (MBC) at 3,700m with awe-inspiring close-up views of the sacred Fishtail Peak. This is one of the most dramatic landscape reveals in all of Himalayan trekking.
day_by_day.afternoon: Final ascent to Annapurna Base Camp (ABC) at 4,130m — the sacred inner sanctuary surrounded by a complete 360-degree ring of Himalayan giants: Annapurna I (8,091m — 10th highest peak on Earth), Annapurna South, Gangapurna, Glacier Dome, Khangsar Kang, and Machhapuchhre. Spend the afternoon exploring the glacier moraines and taking in the overwhelming scale of the amphitheater.
day_by_day.evening: Sunset at ABC — the light on the surrounding peaks transitions through gold, orange, and deep crimson in a display of extraordinary natural beauty. Premium lodge accommodation at ABC with the best available private rooms. Celebrate reaching the base camp with a special group toast arranged by your guide.

meals.breakfast: Hot breakfast at Deurali before departure
meals.lunch: Packed gourmet lunch box enjoyed at Machhapuchhre Base Camp with the Fishtail Peak towering overhead
meals.dinner: Celebratory ABC dinner: special multi-course teahouse meal with garlic soup, pasta, dal bhat, warm brownie, and hot herbal tea — the guide will arrange a small celebration ceremony

day_by_day.notes: Reaching ABC at 4,130m is the trekking highlight of the entire journey. Altitude effects are common — move slowly, breathe deeply, and rest frequently. If any trekker shows signs of HACE or HAPE (confusion, inability to walk straight, wet cough), immediate descent is mandatory. October weather at ABC is typically stable and clear — temperatures drop to -10°C or below at night. Thermal sleeping bags provided by premium lodge.

day_by_day.morning: Pre-dawn wake-up for the most spectacular sunrise of the entire trip — the first light of dawn illuminating the Annapurna massif from inside the sanctuary is a once-in-a-lifetime experience. Extended guided photography session with professional mountain photographer at the glacier viewpoint.
day_by_day.afternoon: Begin descent from ABC back through Machhapuchhre Base Camp and all the way down to Bamboo (2,310m), benefiting from the rapid altitude reduction and increasing oxygen levels. The descent through the sanctuary gorge offers entirely new perspectives on the landscape seen on the way up.
day_by_day.evening: Arrive Bamboo teahouse lodge. Celebrate the successful ABC summit with a relaxed evening, sharing stories with fellow trekkers. The lower altitude means better sleep and recovery.

meals.breakfast: Hot tea and light snack before sunrise, followed by a full hot breakfast at ABC lodge after sunrise
meals.lunch: Trail lunch at Himalaya Hotel teahouse on the descent — hot soup, fried noodles, and lemon tea
meals.dinner: Bamboo lodge dinner: dal bhat with multiple curries, fresh vegetables, and homemade apple raksi (local spirit) — a well-deserved celebration meal

day_by_day.notes: The descent from 4,130m to 2,310m in one day is approximately 14km and 7–8 hours of trekking. Knees and quads will feel the sustained descent — trekking poles are strongly recommended. The oxygen increase during descent dramatically improves energy and mood — enjoy the feeling! Confirm Day 10 route with guide this evening.

day_by_day.morning: Morning trek from Bamboo back up to Chhomrong (2,170m) via Sinuwa, enjoying the now-familiar forest corridor with fresh eyes and greater appreciation after the ABC experience. Take time to observe wildlife and flora that may have been missed on the ascent.
day_by_day.afternoon: Arrive Chhomrong. Afternoon free time — optional visit to a local Gurung family home for a traditional tea ceremony and cultural exchange arranged by the resort concierge in advance. Learn to cook a traditional Gurung dish with the family.
day_by_day.evening: Final night on the Annapurna trail. Sunset views from Chhomrong's iconic terraces for the last time. The guide will conduct a traditional Nepali blessing ceremony (puja) in gratitude for a safe and successful trek.

meals.breakfast: Full hot breakfast at Bamboo lodge
meals.lunch: Lunch at Sinuwa teahouse — vegetable thukpa (Tibetan noodle soup) and masala tea
meals.dinner: Special farewell trail dinner at Chhomrong's best lodge: multi-course Nepali feast with local Gurung specialties, homemade millet beer (tongba), and traditional sweets

day_by_day.notes: Today is a moderate trekking day of approximately 7km. Use this day for reflection and gratitude — the Annapurna Sanctuary trek is one of the world's great wilderness experiences. Tip your porters and guide today or tomorrow as they will depart after Nayapul. Recommended tip: USD 10–15 per day per porter, USD 15–20 per day for guide.

day_by_day.morning: Final morning on the trail — trek from Chhomrong back down through Jhinu Danda, where natural hot springs await beside the Modi Khola river. A long soak in the geothermal hot springs surrounded by forest is the perfect reward for 7 days of trekking.
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue descent to Nayapul, completing the Annapurna circuit. Private luxury jeep meets the group for the transfer back to Pokhara. Return to Aegean Bliss Resort — check back in to your premium suite, shower, and decompress in pure luxury.
day_by_day.evening: Celebratory return dinner at the resort. Arrange for a traditional Nepali Thangka painting or handicraft souvenir to be presented to the trekking team. Relaxing evening at the resort spa with a full post-trek recovery treatment.

meals.breakfast: Hot breakfast at Chhomrong lodge before final descent
meals.lunch: Celebratory trail-end lunch at a Nayapul restaurant — fresh dal bhat, mixed curries, and cold Everest beer (the first cold beer in a week!)
meals.dinner: Luxury return dinner at the resort: full five-course tasting menu celebrating the completion of the Annapurna trek with Himalayan trout, yak tenderloin, and a special dessert platter

day_by_day.notes: The Jhinu Danda hot springs are approximately 20 minutes off the main trail — absolutely do not skip this. Bring a towel and change of clothes. The spring temperature is approximately 40°C. Upon return to the resort, a post-trek recovery package including massage, steam bath, and physiotherapy is highly recommended and should be pre-booked with the concierge.

day_by_day.morning: Full rest and recovery morning at the resort. Sleep in, enjoy a leisurely breakfast, and use the resort's premium wellness facilities — infinity pool, sauna, steam room, and hydrotherapy suite. Optional gentle stretching class with the resort's yoga instructor to aid muscle recovery.
day_by_day.afternoon: Private guided cultural excursion to the Tibetan Refugee Camp and craft center in Pokhara — visit the carpet weaving workshops, meet Tibetan artisans, and purchase premium hand-knotted Tibetan carpets, thangka paintings, and turquoise jewelry as luxury souvenirs. Followed by a visit to the International Mountain Museum — the world's finest museum dedicated to Himalayan mountaineering history.
day_by_day.evening: Sunset sailing on Phewa Lake aboard a private luxury boat with champagne and canapés. Watch the Annapurna range glow in the last light of day from the water — a beautifully contrasting perspective after trekking through those very mountains.

meals.breakfast: Indulgent resort breakfast in bed: freshly squeezed juices, eggs cooked to order, artisan pastries, local honey, and premium Nepali coffee
meals.lunch: Lakeside lunch at Pokhara's finest restaurant — Caffe Concerto or equivalent — featuring Italian-Nepali fusion cuisine with lake views
meals.dinner: Private candlelit dinner on the resort's floating pontoon on Phewa Lake: six-course tasting menu with wine pairing, featuring the best of Himalayan and international cuisine

day_by_day.notes: This is a designated recovery day — resist the urge to over-schedule activities. Your body needs rest after 8 days of high-altitude trekking. The International Mountain Museum is genuinely world-class and provides wonderful context for the trek you have just completed. Museum admission is included in the premium package.

day_by_day.morning: Private chartered helicopter flight from Pokhara to the Mustang region or a scenic mountain circuit flight over Dhaulagiri, Annapurna, and Manaslu — the ultimate aerial perspective of the range you trekked through. Land at a remote mountain viewpoint for a champagne breakfast with the Himalayas as a backdrop.
day_by_day.afternoon: Return helicopter flight to Pokhara. Afternoon at leisure — optional white-water rafting on the Seti River (Class III rapids, suitable for all levels) or a guided paragliding flight over Phewa Lake and the Annapurna foothills with a certified tandem pilot — Pokhara is considered one of the world's top paragliding destinations.
day_by_day.evening: Premium shopping experience in Pokhara's Lakeside district with a personal shopping guide — curated selection of luxury Nepali handicrafts, pashmina shawls, hand-beaten singing bowls, and custom-made trekking gear. Followed by a sunset cocktail hour at the resort.

meals.breakfast: Champagne and gourmet breakfast at the mountain helicopter landing point
meals.lunch: Lunch at a premium Pokhara restaurant post-helicopter return — Pokhara Grande Hotel's restaurant or equivalent fine dining
meals.dinner: Final Pokhara dinner at the resort with a special Himalayan chef's table experience: watch the head chef prepare a traditional Newari feast with live cooking demonstration and storytelling about Nepali culinary heritage

day_by_day.notes: The helicopter flight is weather-dependent — October is statistically the best month for helicopter operations in Nepal with 90%+ clear day probability. Paragliding flights typically last 30–45 minutes and depart from Sarangkot Hill. Both activities require advance booking through the resort concierge. Weight limits apply for helicopter flights — check with operator.

day_by_day.morning: Final sunrise from the resort terrace — one last golden view of the Annapurna range before departure. Leisurely breakfast with time for personal reflection, journal writing, or final photography of the lake and mountains. Pack and prepare for checkout.
day_by_day.afternoon: Private luxury transfer from the resort to Pokhara Airport for the domestic flight to Kathmandu, or direct chartered helicopter transfer to Kathmandu if preferred. Upon arrival in Kathmandu, optional 3-hour curated farewell tour of Pashupatinath Temple and Boudhanath Stupa — two of Asia's most sacred sites — with a private guide before airport transfer.
day_by_day.evening: Private luxury transfer to Tribhuvan International Airport for departure flight. Resort concierge will have pre-arranged airport fast-track service, premium lounge access, and a farewell gift package including Nepali tea, local honey, and a hand-painted Thangka miniature as a memory of the Annapurna journey.

meals.breakfast: Grand farewell breakfast at the resort: the full luxury spread — every item from the menu — as a final celebration of an extraordinary 14-day Himalayan journey
meals.lunch: Farewell lunch at Kathmandu's finest restaurant — Dwarika's Hotel restaurant or Krishnarpan — featuring the definitive Newari royal feast experience
meals.dinner: Airport lounge dining or in-flight meal — the resort will prepare a luxury farewell snack box with Nepali sweets, local nuts, and artisan tea for the journey home

day_by_day.notes: Ensure all trekking permits, ACAP cards, and TIMS cards are retained as souvenirs — they make wonderful mementos.
